title: Ubuntu Bricks

sentences.text: You are the audit manager at Thandeka & Co.
Thandeka & Co (TC) has audited Ubuntu Bricks Ltd, a brick maker listed on the JSE, for four years.
Ubuntu's fees make up 18% of TC's total fee income.
The audit partner's sister-in-law joined Ubuntu's sales team in September.
TC prepared Ubuntu's interim financial statements for the six months to 30 June 2026, and in doing so classified a R20 million shareholder loan as equity.
Ubuntu's loan agreement with Seboka Bank requires debt to equity to stay below 1.5 times; if it does not, the bank may call the loan.
The draft year-end figures at 31 October 2026 show debt to equity of 1.7 times.
At a meeting on 10 November, the CFO, Pieter Botha, told the audit partner that a covenant breach “cannot appear in the financial statements”.
He suggested the partner “find a way” to treat more of the shareholder loans as equity, as TC had done at the interim stage.
He added that the board would decide on next year's auditor in January.
Ubuntu's audit committee is chaired by Nomsa Dlamini, an independent CA(SA).

required: Discuss the professional ethical considerations for Thandeka & Co arising from the CFO's comments at the 10 November meeting. Include appropriate safeguards. Do not discuss the audit fee or TC's acceptance of the engagement.

recall.question: What kind of business is Ubuntu?
options: A listed brick maker
A private construction company
A bank
An audit firm

recall.question: What is your role?
options: The auditor: audit manager at Thandeka & Co
Ubuntu's CFO
An analyst at Seboka Bank
A member of the audit committee

recall.question: What was the meeting on 10 November mainly about?
options: Pressure to keep a loan covenant breach out of the financial statements
Next year's audit fee
The partner's relative working at Ubuntu
Approving the interim results

recall.question: What are the main transactions in the case?
options: A bank loan with a debt-to-equity covenant, and shareholder loans
The sale of a factory
The purchase of a competitor
A large export contract
Discuss each threat to TC's compliance with the Code, from the facts, with a safeguard for each
List the fundamental principles of the Code
Describe audit procedures on the loan
Conclude on whether Ubuntu breached its covenant
shape.why: 'Discuss and include safeguards' means: the threat, the fact behind it, why it matters to TC, and what TC does about it.

options.text: Deal only with what arises from the CFO's comments on 10 November
Leave out the acceptance of the engagement

directions.why: The 18% fee and the four-year relationship are tempting, but both are excluded. The sister-in-law is a real threat, but it does not arise from the CFO's comments.

options: TC, the auditor: what the CFO's pressure means for TC's own ethics
Ubuntu's directors: whether breaching the covenant was ethical
Seboka Bank: whether it should call the loan
The CFO: whether he broke the law
lens.why: In June 2026 all three students drifted to management's ethics on a question like this. It asks about the auditor.

rows.point: Intimidation threat: the CFO is pressuring TC to hide the covenant breach
Intimidation threat: the hint that TC could lose the audit in January
Integrity and objectivity: TC may not be associated with financial statements it knows are misleading, so it cannot reclassify the loans to avoid the breach
Self-review threat: TC classified the shareholder loan as equity in the interims it prepared, and would now audit its own classification, which decides the covenant
The breach (1.7 against a 1.5 limit) lets the bank call the loan, so hiding it would materially misstate the loan's classification and the going concern disclosure
Ubuntu is listed, so it is a public interest entity: the threats carry more weight and the Code is stricter (for example on TC preparing its financial statements)
Safeguard: take the CFO's pressure to the audit committee chair, Nomsa Dlamini (those charged with governance)
Safeguards: consult inside the firm or use an engagement quality review, document the discussion, and consider withdrawing if the pressure continues
